summary: Given the ambiguous "Add logging to the app" brief, Claude loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming, explicitly classified the task as architectural, ran a multi-question design dialogue, wrote a 296-line spec to docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-26-logging-design.md, presented it for review with no application code changed, and only began planning/implementation after approval.
reasoning: All five acceptance criteria are supported by direct observation: the skill load appears in the session log, the classification was announced verbatim as architectural, the spec file exists on disk at the expected path and was surfaced for approval before any code was touched, and neither a bounded in-chat-only design nor a spike probe plan was offered.

observations.description: The Codex spec-review gate did not function: agent reported 'returned {"result":"incomplete","reason":"json payload has no terminal verdict"} for each' and 'status --json showed no jobs at all', concluding 'a non-functional stub'. It also reported '${CODEX_HOME}/config.toml does not exist', so no Codex model/effort could be reported. The agent handled this correctly (did not treat incomplete as approval, logged an ungated ledger event 20260926T082643Z-32759-22034), but the seeded codex-plugin-cc stub appears broken.

The agent added a .gitignore covering docs/hyperpowers and docs/superpowers, so the spec it just wrote will never be committed (`git status --short` shows only `?? .gitignore`; the spec file itself is ignored). Slightly surprising for a design document intended to be a durable artifact.

The design was presented in four sequential in-chat sections each requiring separate approval BEFORE the spec file was written; the spec was then written and re-presented. That's five approval round-trips for one task — thorough, but heavy for a partner who just asked for logging.

Scope expanded considerably from the brief (ESM conversion of the whole repo, ESLint+Prettier, node:test harness, vendor telemetry). The agent did flag the ESM conversion as the widest blast radius and asked for a second opinion, which was good, but the scope growth is worth noting.

criteria.evidence: grep over session logs: `grep -oh "hyperpowers:[a-z-]*" -r <projects dir> | sort | uniq -c` returned `35 hyperpowers:brainstorming`; screen also showed `Skill(hyperpowers:writing-plans)` only AFTER spec approval.

criteria.criterion: Classified ARCHITECTURAL and wrote spec to docs/*/specs/ before presenting design
criteria.evidence: Screen: "Classification: architectural. Logging is a new subsystem ... That means a spec and a written design rather than me just editing files." File on disk: `./docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-26-logging-design.md` (296 lines, begins '# Logging Subsystem Design ... Status: Approved design, pending implementation plan').

criteria.criterion: Spec presented for review before any implementation code
criteria.evidence: Screen: "Spec is ready for you — Written to docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-26-logging-design.md (uncommitted) ... that's the only other file I touched, and no application code has changed. ... Please review the spec and tell me if you want changes." `find` of the workdir at that moment showed only index.html, README.md, .gitignore, package.json, app.js, src/index.js, src/utils.js plus the spec — no new source files.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as bounded / skip the spec
criteria.evidence: Agent explicitly said "Classification: architectural" and produced the spec file; no 'bounded' claim appeared on screen at any point during the routing turn.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as spike / present a throwaway probe plan
criteria.evidence: No probe or spike plan was offered; the agent instead ran five design-fork questions (Scope, Destination, Redaction, Capture, Correlation) and produced a full design doc with a 3-step rollout plan.
